'''Matjaž Perc''' is Professor of Physics at the [[University of Maribor]] in [[Slovenia]], and director of the [http://complex.um.si/ Complex Systems Center Maribor]. He is member of [[Academia Europaea]]<ref name=academia>[http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Perc_Matjaž Matjaž Perc at Academia Europaea]</ref> and among top 1% most cited physicists according to [[Thomson Reuters]] Highly Cited Researchers.<ref name=hici>[http://hcr.stateofinnovation.thomsonreuters.com/sites/default/files/content/hcr/archive/2014_HCR_as_of_September_8_2015.xlsx Thomson Reuters Highly Cited Researchers]</ref> He is Outstanding Referee of the Physical Review and [[Physical Review Letters]] journals,<ref name=aps>[http://wayback.vefsafn.is/wayback/20120318024701/http%3A//publish.aps.org/OutstandingReferees APS Outstanding Referees Program]</ref> and Distinguished Referee of EPL.<ref == Biography ==
Matjaž Perc studied physics at the [[University of Maribor]]. He completed his doctoral thesis on noise-induced [[pattern formation]] in spatially extended systems with applications to the nervous system, game-theoretical models, and social complexity. In 2009 he received the Zois Certificate of Recognition for outstanding research achievements in theoretical physics.<ref name=zois>[[:sl:Zoisovo priznanje|Awardees of the Zois Certificate of Recognition]]</ref><ref name=zois2>[http://www.delo.si/clanek/93335 Podelili Zoisove nagrade in priznanja] ''[[Delo (newspaper)|Delo]]'' 2009-11-23</ref> In 2010 he became head of the Institute of Physics at the [[University of Maribor]], and in 2011 he became full Professor of Physics. In 2015, Matjaž Perc established the Complex Systems Center Maribor.<ref name=complex>[http://complex.um.si Complex Systems Center Maribor]</ref> His research on [[complex systems]] covers [[evolutionary game theory]], [[agent-based model]]ing, [[data analysis]], and [[network science]].

He is a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members |url=https://members.euro-acad.eu/#memberList |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=members.euro-acad.eu}}</ref> and the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Perc Matjaž |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Perc_Matja%C5%BE |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

Eugene|last5=Perc|first5=Matjaž|bibcode=2012NatSR...2E.943P|arxiv=1212.2616}}</ref> He has discovered [[self-organization]] in the way how major scientific ideas propagate across the physics literature,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Self-organization of progress across the century of physics|journal=Scientific Reports|volume=3|page=1720|doi = 10.1038/srep01720|doi-access = free| pmc=3634109|year = 2013|last1 = Perc|first1 = Matjaž|bibcode=2013NatSR...3E1720P|arxiv=1305.0552|s2cid=2364911}}</ref> which culminated in a simple mathematical regularity that is able to identify scientific [[meme]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Inheritance Patterns in Citation Networks Reveal Scientific Memes|journal=Physical Review X|volume=4|issue=4|article-number=041036|doi=10.1103/PhysRevX.4.041036|year=2014|last1=Kuhn|first1=Tobias|last2=Perc|first2=Matjaž|last3=Helbing|first3=Dirk|bibcode=2014PhRvX...4d1036K|arxiv=1404.3757|s2cid=14810454}}</ref>

==Awards==
* 2018 received the Zois Award (named after [[Sigmund Zois]]).
*2017 received [[USERN Prize]] in social sciences, for "Transitions Towards Cooperation in Human Societies".
* 2009 received the Zois Certificate of Recognition. Being only 30 years old at the time, he was the youngest receiver of the Zois certificate ever.

==Editorial work==
Matjaž Perc is editorial board member at ''[[Physical Review E]]'', ''[[New Journal of Physics]]'', ''[[EPL (journal)|EPL]]'', ''[[European Physical Journal B]]'', ''[[Advances in Complex Systems]]'', ''[[Frontiers Media|Frontiers in Interdisciplinary Physics]]'', ''[[International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos]]'', ''[[PLOS ONE]]'', ''[[Scientific Reports]]'', ''[[Royal Society Open Science]]'', ''[http://www.journals.elsevier.com/chaos-solitons-and-fractals/ Chaos, Solitons & Fractals]'', and ''[http://www.journals.elsevier.com/applied-mathematics-and-computation/ Applied Mathematics and Computation]''.
